Original experience of a thriller/investigation-game through a phone.
It is a game played in a voyeuristic way where you have to explore somebody-else´s privacy to investigate on her disappearance (here, a pretty girl, how convenient), instead of just giving the phone to the police.
Firstly reluctant of this voyeurism, the game became for me captivating in a way that I couldn't stop playing it until the very end... We are driven more and more into a frightening suspense, which leads to a very lazy conclusion... :/

It was an interesting experience. A unique idea, with a bit of trouble in presentation. The whole "You're on a smart phone" idea is great, but, as video games /usually/ forego the annoying/monotonous things about real life (even simulators), you may find yourself saying, "ALRIGHT GET ON WITH IT" as text message after text message appears. I look forward to seeing how they've built further on these ideas in the sequel. As far as the story...it was weird. I don't know how to feel about it. I think the game may rely on a bit /too/ many hard-to-find details/easter eggs to round out the experience. There are some puzzle elements, but with a bit of sleuthing and applying situations to real life, you can make it through without scratching your head for too long. 6/10, but lots of potential.

Simulacra is a game with a simple quirk the lends itself to PAGES worth of unpacking: using someone's phone to learn about them, and ultimately help them. While Simulacra bills itself as a horror game, I honestly see it as more of a high-concept thriller. The idea that you can learn so much about someone from their unlocked phone isn't new, but to see it demonstrated so effectively is shocking. 5/5

The design of the game is really good, the overall feel of the game had a creepy tone with sound and visual effects which I really liked and I think it fits really well. There were several endings and some of the choices you make matter a lot. The gameplay, sound design and graphics were really nice. 

The game has game+ feature which is a neat thing to have with these several ending games, it makes the text speed a lot faster so you can easily reach to the point where everything matters. Overall it was a great experience and I highly recommend playing it.

I have never played this kind of simulation game before. I also liked this game because I like escape games. There are multiple endings. I can say that it is not very difficult and it is a short game. The game drags you towards an end according to your choices. I don't think the level of fear is too much. There are a few small jumpscares. Maybe it would be better if you turn the volume all the way up. But still not enough for a horror game. But I recommend this game because I like this kind of escape games and it is not boring. You wonder what will happen after the moves you make, and you wonder how you will reach the other endings and what will happen. Also, this is one of the reasons I recommend the game. And finally, I can say that I like the story.
